To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we generated a novel approach for the safe exploitation, through suicide gene therapy, of the alloreactivity of human memory T cells.
suicide gene-modified central memory human T cells cultured with interleukin-7 and interleukin-15 are as alloreactive as unmodified T cells and can be used to treat leukemia.
the combination of IL-15 and IL-7 allows the generation of self-renewing suicide gene-modified human central memory T lymphocytes with potent antileukemia and alloreactive properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a safe and effective therapy to treat patients with leukemia, based on the use of alloreactive human T lymphocytes that can be eliminated if they cause GVHD.
the generation of suicide genes modified alloreactive self renewing central memory human lymphocytes.
the development of a novel approach for the treatment of hematological malignancies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

suicide gene-modified human T cells cultured with the cytokine combination IL-7 and Il-15, retain the ability to differentiate into alloreactive effectors, and are as efficient as unmanipulate T cells.
IL-7 and/or IL-15 allow for the generation of self-renewing suicide gene-modified central memory human T cells with potent antileukemia activity.
the combination of IL-15 and IL-7 is a potent and safe way to generate suicide gene-modified human alloreactive central memory T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of IL-15 and IL-7 allows the generation of suicide-modified central memory T cells that can be used to treat leukemia patients.
the use of suicide genes in gene therapy for GVHD can be improved by using T(CM) rather than T(EM) lymphocytes and by using a cocktail of IL-7 plus IL-15 rather than IL-2.
suicide gene-modified central memory human T cells can self-renew, persist and differentiate into effector memory human T cells in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generation of suicide genes-modified T cells with the ability to self-renew is a key step to achieve the clinical benefit of allogeneic T cell therapies.
the use of IL-7/IL-15 allows the generation of suicide-modified alloreactivity human T cells that are as potent as unmodified cells in causing GVHD and that can self-renew upon antigen stimulation.

the use of a combination of IL7 and IL15 in vitro allows the generation of alloreactive self-sustaining central memory T lymphocytes that can be used to treat leukemia patients after allogeneictic transplantation.
